q: What does a cone snail use as a harpoon to inject venom into its prey?
choices: A spine on the edge of its shell
A stinger at the tip of its foot
explain: Cone snails fire a hollow, harpoon-like tooth from their radula, the toothed feeding ribbon, and push venom through it to paralyze prey.

source.title: Predatory and Defensive Strategies in Cone Snails - PMC

searchNote: Review describes cone snails using a modified radula tooth shaped like a hollow harpoon, delivered ballistically, to inject a cocktail of peptide neurotoxins into prey.

q: The geographic cone snail of the Indo-Pacific is best known for what?
choices: A sting that can be fatal to people
A shell that glows in the dark
explain: The geographic cone's venom is potent enough to kill a person, which is why divers and beachcombers are warned not to handle live cone snails.

q: Cone snail venom is a mix of many small nerve-blocking molecules known as what?
explain: Conotoxins are short peptides, small chains of amino acids, that jam the signals nerves use, quickly paralyzing a cone snail's prey.

source.title: Predatory and Defensive Strategies in Cone Snails - PMC

source2.title: Cone Snail Toxicity - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf - NIH

searchNote: Sources say cone snail venom contains hundreds of different compounds called conotoxins that interfere with nerve impulses and paralyze prey.

q: Ziconotide, a medicine made as a copy of a cone snail venom molecule, is approved to treat what?
explain: Ziconotide, sold as Prialt, is a lab-made version of a toxin from the magician cone snail. It is reserved for severe pain when other treatments fail.

source.title: Ziconotide - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf - NIH

source2.title: Ziconotide: a review of its pharmacology and use in the treatment of pain - PMC

searchNote: StatPearls: ziconotide (Prialt) is a synthetic version of omega-conotoxin MVIIA from the fish-hunting cone snail Conus magus, FDA-approved for severe chronic pain when other options fail.

q: Unlike morphine, the cone-snail-derived painkiller ziconotide works by blocking what?
explain: Ziconotide plugs N-type calcium channels, tiny gates that pain-sensing nerves need to pass on signals, and it does not act on opioid receptors.

source.title: Ziconotide: neuronal calcium channel blocker for treating severe chronic pain - PubMed

source2.title: Ziconotide - StatPearls - NCBI Bookshelf - NIH

searchNote: PubMed title calls ziconotide a neuronal calcium channel blocker; StatPearls says it blocks N-type calcium channels in the spinal cord and does not bind opioid receptors.

q: How does the fish-hunting magician cone snail (Conus magus) detect a nearby fish?
choices: By sensing chemicals in the water

searchNote: Review says species such as Conus magus detect fish with chemosensors, then extend the proboscis to impale the fish with a hollow, venom-filled harpoon-like tooth.

q: What mainly focuses the image in a scallop's eye?
choices: A curved mirror at the back of the eye
A thick crystal lens at the front
explain: Scallop eyes work like reflecting telescopes: a concave mirror at the back of each eye reflects light onto the retina to form an image.

q: The mirror inside each scallop eye is built from tiny square tiles of what?

Along the edge of its mantle

q: Research on the sea slug Aplysia helped Eric Kandel win a Nobel Prize for discoveries about what?
choices: How memories form at connections between nerve cells
How the immune system fights infection
explain: Kandel showed that learning strengthens synapses, the junctions between nerve cells, and that long-term memory needs new proteins. He shared the 2000 Nobel Prize.

source2.title: Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2000

q: Which simple reflex in the sea slug Aplysia did Eric Kandel study to learn how memory works?
choices: Pulling in its gill when touched
Flipping over when turned upside down
explain: Aplysia's gill-withdrawal reflex grows stronger after a strong stimulus, and Kandel traced that simple form of learning to changes at the synapses.

source.title: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2000 - Press release - NobelPrize.org

searchNote: Nobel press release: Aplysia has a gill-withdrawal reflex; amplification of the reflex was treated as learning and traced to strengthened synapses between sensory and motor neurons.

q: Why was the sea slug Aplysia a good choice for studying learning?
choices: It has relatively few nerve cells, and many are large
Its nerve cells glow under ultraviolet light
